
[38;5;174m ▐[48;5;16m▛███▛█[39m[49m   [1mClaude Code[0m [38;5;246mv2.1.263
[38;5;174m▝▜[48;5;16m█████[49m█▀[39m  [38;5;246mOpus 5 with high effort · Claude Max
[38;5;174m  ▝▝ ▝▝  [39m  [38;5;246m~/repos/DevOfPie/Mustur

[39m  [1mUpdated to latest. Got 8 features, 39 bugfixes, and 19 other changes.
[0m  [38;5;246m]8;id=1rmwg0m;https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog\code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog]8;;\ for details

[2m[39m▎[0m [38;5;246mUsing Opus 5 (from managed settings) · /model

[38;5;239m[48;5;237m❯ [38;5;231mReview Mustur and the deployment and validate that it will remain secure if I remove the [39m         
  [38;5;231mCloudflare application access. Flag any concerns that need to be handled before access is [39m        
  [38;5;231mremoved. You should be able to locally access the UI rather tan testing it through the secured [39m   
  [38;5;231mdomain.[39m                                                                                           

[49m  [38;5;246mSearched for [1m15[0m[38;5;246m patterns, read [1m3[0m[38;5;246m files, listed [1m2[0m[38;5;246m directories, called mustur, ran [1m38[0m[38;5;246m shell commands
[39m  [38;5;246m [39m                                                                                                 
                                                                                                    
[38;5;231m●[39m Tested against a local copy of the production store ([38;5;153m--sessions --origin --accounts[39m, same flags as
  the deployed unit), not through the domain.                                                       
                                                                                            
  [1mVerdict[0m                                                                        
                        
  No — two things must be fixed first. Both are small. Everything else holds up better than I
  expected.

  [1mBlockers

[0m  [1m1. [38;5;153mPOST /intake[39m and [38;5;153mPOST /questions[39m have no origin check.[0m They are the only two write routes that
  don't call [38;5;153msameOrigin(r)[39m — [38;5;153minternal/web/intake.go:64[39m, [38;5;153minternal/web/questions.go:96[39m. Proven: a
  cross-origin POST carrying a valid owner cookie filed [38;5;153mIDW-F-0006[39m into the store and exported it.

  The [38;5;153m/questions[39m one is the sharp end. An answer is typed into the running session — [38;5;153mMUS-Q-0079
[39m  carries [38;5;153mDelivered: typed into mustur/Check[39m — so a forged answer is attacker-chosen text into a
  live agent's stdin.

  The only thing stopping it today besides Access is [38;5;153mSameSite=Lax[39m, and Lax is [3msite[0m-scoped, not
  origin-scoped. Any page on any [38;5;153m*.devofpie.com[39m host is same-site and its POST carries the Mustur
  cookie. LinkCtrl is on the same tunnel and the same zone. Right now Access refuses that request
  before Mustur sees it; remove Access and it arrives. Fix is one call each — the function is right
  there and every other POST uses it.

  [1m2. [38;5;153mCf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email[39m is trusted unconditionally, with no check that Access is in 
[0m  [1mfront.[0m Four call sites: [38;5;153mintake.go:347[39m, [38;5;153mcompose.go:83[39m, [38;5;153mquestions.go:111[39m, [38;5;153msessions.go:138[39m. It is
  preferred over everything else. [38;5;153mdocs/ingress.md[39m records that cloudflared passes client headers
  through. Proven: [38;5;153mIDW-F-0007[39m is filed as [38;5;153mceo@bigcorp.example[39m on the strength of that header alone.

  With Access gone nothing trustworthy ever sets it, so it becomes pure forgery — the record log, an
  answer's provenance, and what gets typed into an agent all wear a name the requester picked. That
  is precisely what MUS-D-0126 exists to stop. The actor should come from [38;5;153mAuth.Whoever[39m once
  [38;5;153m--accounts[39m is on, and the header ignored.

  [1mShould fix, not blocking

[0m  - [1mNo [38;5;153mX-Frame-Options[39m / [38;5;153mframe-ancestors[39m, anywhere.[0m Cross-site framing is already dead (Lax
    withholds the cookie), but a same-site sibling can frame [38;5;153m/sessions/<p>[39m [3mwith[0m the cookie and
    clickjack the key row or the new stop button. One header on the shell.
  - [1mA sole owner cannot revoke their own session.[0m [38;5;153mEndSession[39m deletes only the browser that asks.
    Sessions do get dropped on [38;5;153mDisable[39m ([38;5;153maccount.go:499[39m), but the people screen refuses to disable
    the last owner and the CLI has no [38;5;153mdisable[39m at all — cases are
    invite/list/token/tokens/revoke/grant. So: stolen cookie, 30-day sliding expiry, no supported
    lever. Fine while Access is the outer gate; not fine when it isn't.
  - [1mNo CSP on the HTML surfaces.[0m There's no XSS I can find — the terminal screen reaching [38;5;153minnerHTML
[39m    ([38;5;153msession.js:146[39m) is correctly escaped in [38;5;153minternal/ansi/ansi.go[39m, styles are built from parsed
    ints against a fixed palette, and attachments are refused unless PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP then served
    [38;5;153mnosniff[39m + [38;5;153mdefault-src 'none'; sandbox[39m. CSP is what keeps the [3mnext[0m one from being total on a page
    that types into an agent.
  - [1m[38;5;153mPOST /signin/begin[39m is public and writes a row per call.[0m Bounded (5-minute life, swept on each
    insert), but it's the only unauthenticated path to disk. Belongs in Cloudflare rate limiting,
    not Go. Related: the server sets [38;5;153mReadHeaderTimeout[39m and no write/idle timeout.
  - [1m[38;5;153m/healthz[39m is public and prints the record count.[0m Trivial, and it does become a size oracle for
    strangers once the 302 is gone.
  - [1m[38;5;153mPOST /account/invite[39m honours a [38;5;153mproject[39m form field while [38;5;153mowns()[39m only checks [38;5;153ma.Project[39m.[0m Changes
    nothing on a one-project install; it's a hole waiting for the second.

  [1mWhat actually holds

[0m  The guard wraps the whole mux, not per-handler. Measured every surface unauthenticated: 303 to
  sign-in or 403, no leaks, [38;5;153m/mcp[39m 403 without a bearer token. Role separation works — a reader
  account got 403 on [38;5;153m/sessions[39m and [38;5;153m/account/people[39m, 200 on [38;5;153m/records[39m. Session, invitation and agent
  secrets are 32 random bytes with only the SHA-256 stored. Passkeys are origin-bound, discoverable
  required, backup flags stored, verification in [38;5;153mgo-webauthn[39m. [38;5;153msameOrigin[39m refuses a missing or [38;5;153mnull
[39m  Origin, so it survives a sandboxed frame. One [38;5;153mexec.CommandContext[39m in the tree, args slice, no
  shell — and the start form submits neither a path nor a command, only a record id and an allowlist
  entry.

  Removing the Access application does not expose port 7777: [38;5;153mloopbackOnly[39m refuses any other address
  and the tunnel still terminates TLS and fronts the DDoS.

  [1mYours to check, Cloudflare side

[0m  Whether removing the Access application also removes the zone's WAF and rate limiting — Mustur has
  none of its own. Whether the zone sets HSTS (cookies are [38;5;153mSecure[39m, so a downgrade loses the session
  rather than leaking it, but the first request is still plaintext without it). And what else can
  host a page on [38;5;153mdevofpie.com[39m — that premise is what makes blockers 1 and 3 real rather than
  theoretical.

  I can fix 1 and 2 now; they're a few lines each. Want the six lower-priority ones filed as
  findings in Mustur?
